notes: Contraction mirror of biology-replace-0016. The revision edit is derived (the structure of DNA was discovered in Canada, from the discoverers and their workplace), so the contraction removes its main stored premise: the structure of DNA was discovered by James Watson and Francis Crick. Relation: has_discoverer, shared with biology-delete-0015 (new, functional, staged), inverse discoverer_of. The cardinality question asks Charles Darwin as another candidate ('no' before, 'does not know' after). Related near is the inverse; related far binds the structure through 'the double helix'. The derived questions pick one of the two discoverers by nationality and look up a fact stored about him by name (Watson's birthplace, Crick's birth year); the nationality in the description is part of identifying the person from the removed fact, so the question stays at the edit plus one stored fact. Questions about the Cavendish Laboratory, Cambridge or the 1962 Nobel Prize were dropped: the structure of DNA is stored as a discovery of the Cavendish Laboratory and of the 1962 prize independently of the pair, which would keep a route alive. related[1]: functional, the removed fact asked as yes/no (has_discoverer is functional); the paired revision (a derived edit on discovery_country) has only one related query, so this mirrors the removed fact rather than a revision query.
